annual_report_facts.statement: Kaynes Technology operates predominantly in the business segment of Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS) providing integrated end-to-end design and manufacturing solutions.
Domestic revenue reached ₹32,752.70 Million (~90.3% of total revenue) while Outside India export revenue stood at ₹3,510.84 Million (~9.7%).
FY 2025-26 Consolidated Revenue from Operations reached ₹36,263.54 Million, up 33.2% YoY from ₹27,217.52 Million in FY25.
FY 2025-26 Consolidated Profit Before Tax stood at ₹5,043.14 Million, up from ₹3,716.24 Million in FY25.
FY 2025-26 Consolidated Profit After Tax (PAT) reached ₹3,638.90 Million (~10.0% net margin), up 24.0% YoY from ₹2,934.33 Million.
Shareholders' Total Equity expanded to ₹47,624.88 Million as of 31st March 2026, up from ₹28,442.32 Million.
Consolidated Short-term borrowings stood at ₹5,379.41 Million as of 31st March 2026.
Net cash from operating activities was negative ₹6,004.04 Million (-₹600.4 Cr) due to large working capital absorption (Receivables increase of ₹10,238.66 Mn).
Corporate Guarantees extended to Subsidiary Companies stood at ₹23,903.60 Million (₹2,390.4 Cr) as of 31st March 2026.
Bank Guarantees for contractual performance of ₹1,905.95 Million, Income tax disputes of ₹130.19 Million, and GST disputes of ₹124.82 Million.

narrative_vs_numbers.topic: Revenue Scale and Growth vs. Operating Cash Flow
narrative_vs_numbers.management_narrative: Management highlights strong revenue performance, such as total revenue reaching INR946 crores with 40% year-on-year growth driven by the EMS business, and FY 2025-26 consolidated revenue reaching ₹36,263.54 Million.
narrative_vs_numbers.reported_numbers: Despite top-line expansion, net cash from operating activities was negative ₹6,004.04 Million due to large working capital absorption, including a receivables increase of ₹10,238.66 Mn.
narrative_vs_numbers.analysis: Rapid top-line growth is severely straining working capital, resulting in negative operating cash flows that diverge from reported profit and revenue growth metrics.

narrative_vs_numbers.topic: Geographic Revenue Mix vs. Global Market Ambitions
narrative_vs_numbers.management_narrative: Management targets global opportunities, pointing to a global PCB market projected to cross USD100 billion by 2030 alongside strong international OSAT order outlooks.
narrative_vs_numbers.reported_numbers: Domestic revenue reached ₹32,752.70 Million representing ~90.3% of total revenue, while Outside India export revenue stood at only ₹3,510.84 Million (~9.7%).
narrative_vs_numbers.analysis: While global aspirations are highlighted, the current revenue mix remains heavily concentrated in the domestic market rather than diversified internationally.

bull_case.title: Strong Top-Line Expansion and Profitability
bull_case.argument: FY 2025-26 Consolidated Revenue from Operations reached ₹36,263.54 Million, representing a robust 33.2% YoY increase from ₹27,217.52 Million in FY25, accompanied by a growing PAT of ₹3,638.90 Million.

bull_case.title: Robust OSAT Order Visibility and Industry Tailwinds
bull_case.argument: The OSAT segment exhibits strong order visibility with over INR25,000 million secured over the next 5 years, supported by broader macroeconomic tailwinds such as India's domestic PCB market growing at a 20% CAGR.

bull_case.title: Expansion of Shareholders' Equity
bull_case.argument: Total shareholders' equity has significantly expanded to ₹47,624.88 Million as of 31st March 2026, up from ₹28,442.32 Million, strengthening the balance sheet foundation.

bear_case.title: Severe Negative Operating Cash Flow and Working Capital Strain
bear_case.argument: Net cash from operating activities was negative ₹6,004.04 Million (-₹600.4 Cr) driven by massive working capital absorption, specifically a receivables increase of ₹10,238.66 Mn.

bear_case.title: Substantial Contingent Liabilities via Corporate Guarantees
bear_case.argument: Corporate Guarantees extended to Subsidiary Companies stood at a significant ₹23,903.60 Million (₹2,390.4 Cr) as of 31st March 2026, exposing the parent entity to material contingent obligations.

bear_case.title: Short-Term Debt and Additional Dispute Exposures
bear_case.argument: Consolidated short-term borrowings stood at ₹5,379.41 Million as of 31st March 2026, compounded by contractual performance bank guarantees of ₹1,905.95 Million alongside ongoing income tax and GST disputes.
